text:
Sam: quick check — following the RFC follow-up: do we have consensus on query stitching crossing RBAC boundaries? Feels like a can of worms for dashboards with mixed-tenancy panels
Maria: I don't think we can allow stitching to fetch across tenant-scoped views without an explicit authz join. security risk
Kevin: +1. Option A: enforce per-panel evaluation and merge results in frontend. Option B: server-side stitched queries that run under a "view service" role with limited columns
Tess: frontend merge increases client bandwidth and latency but is simplest for correctness. server-side stitching is complex for SLOs
Sam: SLOs are key — we already see 99th token latency spikes when panels fanout. Server-side stitching will require careful batching and KV cache changes
Maria: can we do a hybrid? allow server-side stitching only for internal dashboards (org-admins) behind a flag, else frontend merge
Jordan: hybrid seems pragmatic. We should add guardrails: audit logs + rate caps + fallback to separate calls
Kevin: implementation note: if server stitches, it needs to respect RBAC at the row-level. That means authz filters must get pushed into subquery planner. Current query layer's pushdown API is coarse
Tess: so this implies an interface change: PushdownPredicateV2 with per-tenant predicate metadata and a "no-cross-tenant" flag
Sam: yeah. That would be a breaking API for query adapters. We should do an RFC for PushdownPredicateV2 and a 3-phase rollout: adapter opt-in, console enabling flag, default off
Maria: also add regression tests for latency and correctness. we need a perf benchmark simulating 50% mixed-panel dashboards
Jordan: action items: @Kevin write RFC draft, @Tess scope adapter changes, @Sam perf harness + rollout plan, @Maria define guardrail matrix
Kevin: will draft by EOD Friday
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary infra perf harness -> staging at 2024-11-06T09:00Z :white_check_mark:
Sam: thanks. one last thought — we should prefer making stitching explicit in dashboard config (stitch: true) rather than implicit heuristics
Maria: agreed. explicit is safer. we'll add UI opt-in for org-admins
Sam: cool. marking this resolved for now, will follow RFC thread
